distinguishing_fields: 429 + body exactly {status, message} with NO `reason` key and no Retry-After/RateLimit-Policy header. A body that carries `reason` in the fairshare/welcome enum is a different row.
notes: Per the PR author the portal enforces per-key rpm and tph (tokens per hour) limits today and answers with a bare {status,message} 429. Which of rpm or tph fired is only in the (uncaptured) message, so window=unknown. Registry cites community 50 RPM / 500K TPM for Free. No Retry-After documented for this shape: the 20s unsized rule applies. Waiting or another key helps only if the key is not the same Portal account (scope credential, may be account if keys share one subscription).

distinguishing_fields: 429 + body `reason` (fairshare enum) + numeric `retry_after` (+ `alternates`, `upgrade_url`); header RateLimit-Policy: "fairshare" corroborates. Header Retry-After outranks body retry_after.
sources: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/91758 (PR text describing the gateway contract; api repo PRs #143-#147, shadow-mode rollout)
notes: Model-scoped: other Nous models stay available and the key is healthy, so it must not bench the whole credential for every model (R29/R18). Listed `alternates` are the gateway's suggested other models, but the plugin never switches model (closed rule: never swap model). Enum values other than the welcome ones are not enumerated in what was read. The contract was described as upcoming at PR time (shadow rollout); a live capture was not found.

distinguishing_fields: 429 + body.reason == "model_not_free" (or "feature_not_free"): a gate, not a counter. No Retry-After.
notes: Status 429 but the meaning is "this tier never serves this model/feature". Family denial, not throttle: waiting never helps; rotating among anonymous (welcome-tier) credentials is the same tier, so it will not help either. Applies to the anonymous/welcome tier; the plugin's owner is on Portal OAuth or API keys, where this may never occur.

distinguishing_fields: 429 + body.reason in {at_capacity, admission_closed, rate_limited} + retry_after.
sources: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105552 (table: 429 at_capacity / admission_closed / rate_limited -> rate_limit, honours retry_after, falls back)
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105552 (30 rpm profile for the welcome host)
notes: Welcome (anonymous free) tier is counted against a 30 rpm profile per the PR. at_capacity/admission_closed are shared-capacity states, not the caller's counter. retry_after is in the body (whole seconds, 0 when absent).

distinguishing_fields: 404 + body.code == "insufficient_credits_for_paid_model" (and prose "requires available credits"). Status alone (404) says model-not-found; the code says money.
notes: TRAP: a billing wall delivered as 404. A status-first classifier calls it request_fault/model-missing and never rotates. Scope is the account (free models still work on the same key). Waiting does not fix money. The user's ~2-day outage in that issue came from treating it as transient.

distinguishing_fields: 402 status alone (no Nous-specific body found).
sources: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105552 (classifier treats free-tier refusal words as billing)
notes: No captured 402 body from the Nous inference API was found. The credit wall is documented in practice as the 404 above; a plain 402 is the OpenAI-compatible convention only. Inferred.

notes: Welcome-tier cross-refusal. Only reachable if a caller sends an anonymous token to the paid host (or a named token to the welcome host). Exact JSON envelope not captured, so body is a template of the message only.

rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 401/4xx + prose "invalid jwt" on the welcome host: the 15-minute free-tier JWT expired. Refreshable by the host, not a dead key.
sources: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105552 (comment: "retry that waited out a long rate limit outlives the 15-minute free-tier JWT and lands here")
notes: Status code not stated in what was read (the classifier maps by message). OAuth/guest sessions are host-owned and refreshable: strictly this is auth_refresh/defer_host_retry for the guest case, but an API-key credential would be auth_dead. Marked auth_dead only for the generic status; low confidence on the action.

distinguishing_fields: 403 plain "forbidden" body on a Nous route: ambiguous between permission and expired token; no structured code.
sources: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/108022 (that exact string is a Copilot Enterprise case; included only as the generic-403 convention)
notes: Not Nous-specific. No documented Nous 403 for a normal paid account was found. Row kept as the conservative convention; the specific Nous 403 is the anonymous-not-accepted row.

distinguishing_fields: 404 with Content-Type text/plain and body "404 Not Found" (no JSON envelope): an unknown path, not a missing model. A missing model is the JSON-coded 404 above or a 400/404 envelope.
notes: First-hand probe, not a doc page; confidence marked documented because it is the live API's own response. GET /v1/models answers 200 unauthenticated with an OpenRouter-shaped catalog (id, canonical_slug, pricing, per_request_limits), so a 200 from /models says nothing about key validity. Response carries Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Nous-Token-Sharing, a header name only: its meaning is undocumented in what was read.

distinguishing_fields: 5xx status, no structured code.
notes: Host has special copy for "free model outage once retries are spent (5xx, transport failure)". No 5xx body captured. Inferred from the OpenAI convention.

distinguishing_fields: 400 + OpenAI envelope; `param` names the field. Per the fallback guide, invalid requests end the whole fallback list at once.
sources: https://docs.router.com/guides/fallbacks.md ("Invalid requests, model refusals, and content filtering failures end the request immediately")
notes: Exact `type` string for 400 not documented (only the 401 example is). Context-too-long is not separately documented: it would surface as 400 from the provider or as the provider's own status passed through.

rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 401 + error.code == "invalid_api_key". Note the same code also covers an expired key and a key locked by a lifetime spend cap.
sources: https://docs.router.com/api/endpoint.md ("When Router rejects a key, it returns 401 with one of two codes")
notes: TRAP: a spend-cap-locked key returns 401 invalid_api_key (NOT 402), per the 402 row. The key is healthy but locked by its owner's cap; rotating to a sibling key helps only if it has no cap. Message text of the cap case is "explained in the error message" (not captured).

error.message: <reason text, may mention lifetime spend cap>

rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 401 + error.code == "api_key_deactivated" (disabled key, including by lifetime spend cap).
notes: Permanent until a human re-enables the key. Same status/type as invalid_api_key, only `code` differs.

distinguishing_fields: 402 + error.code == "insufficient_credits". Only a plain credit wall; spend-cap locks are 401 instead.
notes: Registry: $26 one-time credits, then list-price billing. type string for 402 not documented, so it is a placeholder.

distinguishing_fields: 403 + error.code == "provider_key_required" (currently Google Gemini models need your own provider key).
notes: Model-scoped denial: other models on the same Router key work. The 403 row also covers "a provider is not currently available" with no distinct code listed; that variant looks identical except for message text.

distinguishing_fields: 404 + error.code == "model_not_found". Docs say it usually means the model is not available to THIS key, even if it exists publicly.
sources: https://docs.router.com/api/errors-and-limits.md ("it usually means that the model is not available for your API key")
notes: Scope is model, but the cause may be key entitlement, so a sibling key could succeed. Closed rule R02 forbids switching model; rotating key within the same model remains allowed, but only one key-class difference can fix it. Conservative: raise_to_host.

distinguishing_fields: 413, body over 100 MiB.
notes: Request-shaped: no key helps. Not a context-window error (that is a provider error).

distinguishing_fields: 429; Router PRESERVES the provider's retry-after and retry-after-ms headers when present. Nothing in the envelope says whether the gateway or a provider produced it.
sources: https://docs.router.com/api/errors-and-limits.md (429 row; "Retries": preserves provider retry-after and retry-after-ms)
notes: Both a provider limit and Router's own limit arrive as 429; the body does not mark which (no `metadata.provider_name` is documented, unlike OpenRouter). With the `models` fallback list the gateway advances itself on provider rate limits before ever returning this. When every candidate failed, Router returns the LAST failure's status/type/code with a suffix "(all N candidates failed: provider:model STATUS code; ...)". Clock units: seconds vs ms, one parser needed (R16).

distinguishing_fields: 500 from Router itself; contact support with x-request-id.
notes: Retry briefly. Headers x-request-id and x-trace-id are echoed (or generated), usable for correlation only.

distinguishing_fields: 501 + error.type == "not_implemented_error": the selected provider cannot represent a requested capability (tools, reasoning, output format). Retrying unchanged will not help.
notes: A 5xx status that is a request fault: must not be mapped to server/rotate. Another model might support it, but the plugin may not switch.

message_template: <PROVIDER> provider request failed. | <PROVIDER> provider response could not be read.
distinguishing_fields: 502 + code provider_request_failed (the provider, not Router, failed). `502 all_candidates_failed` is the variant when no specific last failure can be exposed.
notes: Upstream relay marker here is the code + message template with the provider name, not a metadata object. Same status 502 as an ordinary bad gateway elsewhere.

distinguishing_fields: 503 on Router: "Credentials or pricing data are temporarily unavailable".
notes: Retry later; no Retry-After documented for 503 specifically (Router preserves a provider's if one existed).

message_template: <PROVIDER> provider request failed. (on a deadline) | <PROVIDER> provider response was idle.
distinguishing_fields: 504 + code provider_request_failed; message "response was idle" = stream or response went quiet past provider_timeout.
notes: Timeouts are tunable per request via timeout_before_headers / provider_timeout. Not a key fault.

distinguishing_fields: HTTP 200 stream that ends early with no terminal event: "Once a stream has started, any failures appear as a truncated event stream".
sources: https://docs.router.com/guides/fallbacks.md ("Streaming": Router will not switch models once streaming starts)
notes: No documented SSE error frame. Router also will not fall back after the first token, so a half-delivered answer is the plugin's to stitch or return (R39/R40).

error.message: Parameter <name> ... (see table: "Parameter model is required", "Model <x> is not valid", "Parameter messages can not be empty" ...)

distinguishing_fields: 400 + error.type == "invalid_params". Note: "Model {model} is not valid" is ALSO a 400 invalid_params here while the 404 invalid_model is a separate row.
notes: error.code is the HTTP status as a STRING ("400"), a quirk: do not read it as a provider code.

distinguishing_fields: 413 + error.type == "invalid_params" + message "Prompt is too long": context overflow reported as 413 (not 400).
notes: Context-window overflow. The host should compress, not rotate.

distinguishing_fields: 422 + error.type == "provider_unprocessable_entity_error": request passed ZenMux validation but the upstream provider rejected the structure.
notes: Upstream relay marker: the type name itself. Retrying unchanged is wasted.

rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 403 + error.type == "access_denied". Docs say cause = key invalid, expired or missing; also seen when a key of the wrong SOURCE calls a model (below).
sources: first-hand: owner-measured 2026-10-14 (providers/REGISTRY.md zenmux row): PAYG key got 403 on both free and paid models
notes: TRAP: an invalid key is 403, not 401. Per the owner's measurement the same 403 hits a perfectly valid Pay-As-You-Go key when it asks for the $0 routes (needs a key created with Free source) and when its balance is empty. The error body is the same, so a bad key and a wrong-key-type are not told apart by the response alone (message text not captured for the PAYG case). Action: rotate_key is right for both, but a rest of 300s is wasteful when the key is valid for paid models.

distinguishing_fields: 403 + error.type == "safety_check_failed": input blocked by an upstream safety policy.
notes: Content filter, request fault. Same status as access_denied: only `type` separates them.

distinguishing_fields: structured code insufficient_user_quota (or pre_consume_token_quota_failed), in prose "pre-consume". STATUS VARIES ACROSS new-api deployments: 403 (seen), 402 (seen on OrcaRouter), 400 (seen on b.ai).

The structured code is the only stable evidence, so status-first rules misread it as request fault (400) or denial (403). distinguishing_fields: 429 + error.code == "rate_limit_exceeded" + Retry-After header. Applies only to model ids ending ":free" (all share ONE bucket per account).
notes: TWO counters in one code: 10 requests/minute AND 100 requests/day, shared by every key and every :free model on the account, at any balance. The body does not say which counter fired, only the Retry-After value can (seconds to the next minute vs to the day reset). If Retry-After is large the day cap fired; rotating to another KEY of the SAME account does not help (R08 not applicable unless keys are different accounts). window set per_day as the worse case; unknown which. No x-ratelimit-* headers (docs state none are sent).

distinguishing_fields: 402 + error.code == "insufficient_quota": paid model with balance below 0.05 credits (a 0.05 credit reserve is held per in-flight paid request).
notes: Concurrency of paid requests is limited by balance/0.05, so a "402" can also appear transiently with funds present when many requests run at once (reserve not yet released). Documented as "after a top-up".

distinguishing_fields: 403 + error.code == "credit_limit_exceeded": the KEY's own spending limit (`credit_limit`) is reached, not the account balance.
notes: Billing-family code on a 403 status; scope is the key only: a sibling key without a limit works. Owner-set cap, so a human must raise it.

distinguishing_fields: 403 + error.code == "inappropriate_content" (NagaAI moderation blocked an image prompt).
notes: Moderation, request fault, same status as credit_limit_exceeded; only the code separates them.

distinguishing_fields: 401 + error.type in {authentication_required, invalid_api_key, disabled_api_key, expired_api_key, invalid_provisioning_key, disabled_provisioning_key, account_suspended, account_disabled, account_closed}. On /v1/messages every one is error.type "authentication_error" and only the message differs.
notes: Key prefix ng- + 32 chars. account_suspended/disabled/closed are account-scoped (siblings die too): scope would be account for those three; the table lumps them. invalid_api_key also fires when a provisioning key is sent to a model endpoint.

distinguishing_fields: 400 + error.type == "invalid_request_error". Validation happens BEFORE any provider is picked.
notes: Also 400 unsupported_modality (image to a text-only model).

distinguishing_fields: 400 (not 404) + error.code == "model_not_found". 404 is reserved for unknown PATHS.
notes: TRAP: model-not-found delivered as 400. 410 model_deprecated is the retired-model sibling (request_fault, switch models).

distinguishing_fields: 400 + code content_moderation; OR 400 + message starting "Upstream returned an error: " (documented as a NagaAI conversion bug).
notes: Upstream relay marker = the "Upstream returned an error: " prefix. Both are request-class: do not rotate.

distinguishing_fields: 410 + code model_deprecated.
notes: Retired model. Not a key problem.

distinguishing_fields: 413: body over 32 MiB or one inline part over 20 MiB.
notes: Not a context-window error.

distinguishing_fields: 408: body stopped arriving for 60 s or took over 15 minutes to upload. Documented retry: once.
notes: Client-side slowness.

distinguishing_fields: 422 + code billing_metering_incomplete: the model has no price for an input/output kind in the request (e.g. audio).
notes: Not charged. Change input.

distinguishing_fields: 500 + type server_error ("a bug in NagaAI"; retry once then report).
notes: No Retry-After.

distinguishing_fields: 503 + type server_error; "some 503s" carry Retry-After (load shedding sends Retry-After: 1). A generic 503 after three provider attempts means every provider failed; the request is NOT charged.
notes: This 503 also hides upstream rate limits and exhausted provider quotas (NagaAI retried them across providers, up to three attempts), so an upstream 429 never surfaces as 429 here. Retry-After may be absent: then flat 1s.

distinguishing_fields: HTTP 200 SSE; Chat Completions emits `data: {"error": {...}}` then `data: [DONE]` (Responses: `error` event then response.failed; Messages: `event: error`).
notes: Status is held until the first content is ready, so errors before the first chunk are normal HTTP errors. A stream that fails midway is not charged. Edge limit: >300 requests in 10 s from one IP are blocked for 10 s at the network edge before reaching the API (response shape undocumented).

rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 401 + non-OpenAI body {group, message}: group == "api_key". NO `error` wrapper.
sources: first-hand: unauthenticated GET https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1/models on 2026-10-16 -> 401 {"group":"api_key","message":"API key is required."}
notes: Real capture for a MISSING key. The text for an invalid key was not captured (probably group api_key with a different message). An OpenAI-style client reading body.error finds nothing.

distinguishing_fields: 400 text/plain "Missing model" - not JSON, and it was returned BEFORE any auth check (no key was sent).
sources: first-hand: one unauthenticated POST with body {} to https://api.gmi-serving.com/v1/chat/completions on 2026-10-16 (this single POST departs from the "GET only" brief; no key, no model, no billing)
notes: Errors from the edge/router layer are plain text with Cloudflare headers. A GET on a POST route returns 405 text/plain "Method Not Allowed" (also for unknown paths such as /nope, so unknown path = 405 here, not 404).

distinguishing_fields: 405 text/plain, also returned for UNKNOWN paths.
notes: Misconfigured URL, not rotation material.

distinguishing_fields: 429 on LLM routes. Body, headers and wording not published.
notes: Limits are per ORGANIZATION: TPM for LLMs (Tier 1 1,000,000 TPM; Tier 2 3M after $50 purchase; Tier 3 50M after $500; Tier 4 100M after $1000; "All Models"). RPH (requests per hour) for video models. Sibling keys of one org share it. The page title promises "how to handle 429 responses" but the body has none. No Retry-After documented.

distinguishing_fields: 429 on video endpoints (requests per hour).
notes: Applies to video models only; irrelevant to chat rotation but a 429 on a hour window would be mis-sized by the 20 s rule. Window text not in any body.

distinguishing_fields: 402 status.
sources: https://github.com/RESMP-DEV/ccr-rust/pull/51 ("the ambiguous base Max ID returned 402 with zero balance"; dated free deployment ids are free)
notes: One observation. Body not captured. The same model family had a "dated free deployment ID" that worked at zero balance, so 402 is MODEL-specific on an unfunded account (some ids free, some paid): scope could be model.

distinguishing_fields: Request param context_length_exceeded_behavior = "error" (default "truncate"): overflow fails instead of silently truncating.
notes: DEFAULT is truncate: a context overflow does NOT produce an error unless the caller sets "error". Status for the error mode not documented (400 assumed from convention).

message_template: model <id> is currently inactive and not accepting requests
distinguishing_fields: prose "is currently inactive and not accepting requests" (also unavailable/disabled/deprecated variants).
sources: https://github.com/gratitude5dee/wzrd-studio-desktopfinal/pull/1 (video queue API errors; client detects the phrase)
notes: Seen on the video queue endpoints; status not stated. Treated as model-not-ready for that id. LLM routes may differ. Placed at 400 as a guess flagged community.

distinguishing_fields: 5xx, no structured code.
notes: No GMI 5xx evidence found. Inferred. Registry marks GMI free endpoints as community-documented and unverified.

rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 401 + body {"error": "<string>"} (error is a STRING, not an object) + X-Error-Message header + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.
sources: first-hand: unauthenticated GET https://router.huggingface.co/v1/chat/completions on 2026-10-16 -> 401 (X-Error-Message: Invalid username or password.; body starts {"error":"In...} 41 bytes)
notes: TRAP 1: GET /v1/models answers 200 even with an invalid token ("Bearer hf_invalid" returned 200), so a /models health check cannot validate a key. TRAP 2: a valid token that lacks the fine-grained permission "Make calls to Inference Providers" (or has no credits) also gets 401 on chat completions while /v1/models works (forum thread 174329, analysis by a forum poster, not staff). Body literal is inferred from the 41-byte length and the X-Error-Message header.

body.error: You have exceeded your monthly included credits for Inference Providers. Subscribe to PRO to get 20x more monthly allowance.

message_template: You have exceeded your monthly included credits for Inference Providers. Subscribe to PRO to get 20x more monthly allowance. | ... Pay-as-you-go above your included PRO quota will be available soon.
distinguishing_fields: 402 + body {"error": "<string>"} mentioning "monthly included credits".
sources: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/pricing (free users: no credits; PRO $2/month; pay-as-you-go by purchasing credits)
notes: Text changed over time (older: "Pay-as-you-go ... available soon"; newer: "Subscribe to PRO"). Free accounts have NO included credits, so a free token gets this on first use. Month-scoped (resets monthly) but the plugin has no window label for it: billing family.

body.error: You have reached the free monthly usage limit for <provider>. Add pre-paid credits to your account to continue using <provider>.

message_template: You have reached the free monthly usage limit for <provider>. Add pre-paid credits to your account to continue using <provider>.
distinguishing_fields: 402 + prose "free monthly usage limit for <provider>" (path /<provider>/openai/v1/chat/completions).
notes: Names ONE provider (Groq in the capture). Whether another provider on the same token still works is plausible but not shown. Scope could be model/provider-level; set to account conservatively.

error.message: The requested model '<id>' is not supported by any provider you have enabled.

message_template: The requested model '<id>' is not supported by any provider you have enabled.
distinguishing_fields: 400 + error.code == "model_not_supported" + param "model" (OpenAI envelope, unlike 401/402 which are {"error": string}).
notes: Depends on which providers the USER enabled in settings, so a sibling credential with different provider settings could succeed; with one account it is a model fault. Mixed envelopes within one API.

message_template: v1/chat/completions is not allowed for the hf-inference provider (paraphrase)
distinguishing_fields: 400 on the hf-inference provider path for chat completions.
sources: https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/143956 (forum reply: hf-inference does not accept the OpenAI chat route)
notes: Exact body not captured (search summary only). Low confidence. A routing fault, not a key fault.

distinguishing_fields: 404 on /<provider>/.../chat/completions for models not deployed on that route.
sources: https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/146646 (404 returned for all models during an outage)
notes: TRAP: thread 146646 shows 404 returned for ALL models for a while (an incident), so a 404 can be platform trouble, not a missing model. Exact bodies not captured.

distinguishing_fields: 429 with IETF draft RateLimit / RateLimit-Policy headers (t = seconds to reset). Documented for HUB buckets (api, pages, resolvers), 5-minute fixed windows.
notes: The Hub docs do not mention the Inference Providers router. Whether router.huggingface.co sends these headers on a 429 is UNVERIFIED; no router 429 capture was found. Row kept because the platform standard is one header scheme and `t=` is a stated number. The huggingface_hub >= 1.2.0 client parses RateLimit to wait exact seconds.

distinguishing_fields: 504 on routed/hf-inference calls.
sources: https://discuss.huggingface.co/t/173034 (frequent 504 on the Inference API for a small embedding model; forum reply: not an account limit)
notes: Exact body not captured.

distinguishing_fields: No router-specific marker found for relayed provider failures.
sources: https://github.com/symfony/ai/issues/2671 (chat completion fails with most third-party providers; generic)
notes: The router front for third-party providers (groq, together, fireworks, ...) relays their failures but no documented envelope field marks it (unlike OpenRouter's error.metadata). It cannot be told apart from an HF-owned 5xx by shape alone.

distinguishing_fields: HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/plain and body "OK" on /inference/chat/completions and /catalog/models. A 200 that is not JSON.
sources: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/models/inference ("GitHub Models has been retired", fully retired July 30, 2026)
notes: SURPRISE. The service is gone and the host answers EVERY path and token with 200 "OK". A client reading it gets a JSON parse error (9router logs "Invalid JSON response from github") that a naive classifier will call a transient server fault or empty response. Correct decision: the provider is dead, every credential for it is useless; raise it, never rotate. The registry already lists github-models as ended; a stale config that still points at it will see this shape forever.

body: bad request: missing required Authorization header
message_template: bad request: missing required Authorization header
rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 400 text/plain "bad request: missing required Authorization header": a MISSING key is a 400 here, not 401.
notes: TRAP: missing-credential = 400. The plain-text body has no JSON envelope. Treated as auth_dead because the fault is the credential; a malformed or invalid token text was not captured. GET /chat/completions answers 405 with allow: POST.

error.message: The requested model is not supported.

message_template: The requested model is not supported.
distinguishing_fields: 400 + error.code == "model_not_supported" (+ type invalid_request_error).
notes: The catalog depends on plan and org policy (GET /models lists what a plan serves). A stale id map or a model the plan does not include fails here. Per the rules it must NOT switch model. Another credential (different plan/org) could serve it, so rotation is conceivable, but the response says only "model", so raise_to_host.

rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 403 "forbidden" from an account-specific host (api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com, api.business.githubcopilot.com) when the exchanged Copilot token expired.
notes: TRAP: an expired short-lived token on Enterprise answers 403, not 401. The OAuth/exchanged token is refreshable by the host: family should be auth_refresh/defer_host_retry for a verified refresh route, but nothing in the response proves it is expiry rather than a policy denial (identical 403 "forbidden"). Cannot be taught from the response alone; marked auth_dead as the safe reading and the host's refresh hook should own it.

error.message: <text; may say wait / suggest retry time / upgrade>

distinguishing_fields: errorType "rate_limit" with the fine-grained code: user_model_rate_limited (one model), user_global_rate_limited (all), user_weekly_rate_limited (weekly window), integration_rate_limited (the integration/app), rate_limited (generic). Optional secondsUntilReset field.
sources: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/troubleshoot-copilot/troubleshoot-common-issues.md ("Most people see rate limiting for select models, due to limited capacity ... the error message may tell you to wait ..., suggest a retry time, or prompt you to upgrade")
notes: The SDK event is the SDK's normalized envelope, NOT the raw wire body; where each code sits in the HTTP JSON (and the HTTP status for each) is not confirmed. Scope per code: user_model_rate_limited=model, user_weekly=account weekly window (hours-long: window rolling_unspecified), user_global=account. A weekly or model limit with no stated seconds must not become a long bench without a number (R23). Third-party sources mention x-ratelimit-limit / x-ratelimit-remaining on Copilot 429s; unconfirmed.

distinguishing_fields: code integration_rate_limited: the INTEGRATION (client app id / editor headers) is limited, not the user.
notes: A different user token behind the same integration shares it. Whether rotating helps depends on whether keys share the integration id. Body not captured.

distinguishing_fields: errorType "quota" with errorCode quota_exceeded / session_quota_exceeded / billing_not_configured (CAPI quota error codes).
sources: https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk (nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts, ErrorData) (errorCode doc for errorType quota)
notes: HTTP status NOT confirmed (402 or 429 or 403 are all plausible); it is the code that matters. This is the premium-request allowance running out - billing family, not a counter that resets in minutes. Distinct from rate_limit codes above.

distinguishing_fields: errorType "context_limit" (context window) or "policy" (content/org policy) or "query" (malformed).
sources: https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk (nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts, ErrorData) (errorType categories: authentication, authorization, policy, quota, rate_limit, context_limit, query)
notes: Only the category names are in the SDK; no wire bodies or statuses. Request-class: do not rotate.

distinguishing_fields: 5xx; correlation headers x-github-request-id and x-copilot-service-request-id.
notes: No 5xx bodies captured. Inferred.

distinguishing_fields: The copilot-acp id drives the Copilot CLI over the Agent Client Protocol (a local subprocess), not api.githubcopilot.com.
sources: https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk (nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts, ErrorData) (session.error events, the same errorType/errorCode vocabulary)
notes: No HTTP status exists. Error identity is the SDK event (errorType, errorCode, statusCode?, message). I did not read the Hermes adapter. The decision for each errorType would follow the HTTP rows above.

body.message: No user matching sent API Key. Have you remembered to register at https://stablehorde.net/register ?

message_template: No user matching sent API Key. Have you remembered to register at https://stablehorde.net/register ?
rest_rule: auth: 300s, then 3600 after two refuted re-probes
distinguishing_fields: 401 + body {message, rc:"InvalidAPIKey"}. (Shared-key variant: "No user matching sent Shared Key.")
notes: Horde envelope is {message, rc} with NO `error` wrapper. The anonymous key 0000000000 is valid but low priority.

body.message: Anonymous user is forbidden from performing this operation

message_template: Anonymous user is forbidden from performing this operation
distinguishing_fields: 403 + rc "AnonForbidden".
notes: The anonymous key may not do this operation; a registered key can.

distinguishing_fields: 403 + rc "KudosUpfront": the request would cost more kudos than the user has upfront. Billing-like but 403.
notes: Kudos are the horde's currency, so family billing. Not time-based; a smaller request (fewer tokens/steps) may pass, which is a request-side change. Exact text not extracted.

body.message: Due to abuse prevention, your IP address has been put into timeout for {ttl} more seconds. Please try again later, or contact us on discord if you think this was an error.

message_template: Due to abuse prevention, your IP address has been put into timeout for {ttl} more seconds. ...
distinguishing_fields: 403 + rc in {TimeoutIP, UnsafeIP, TooManyNewIPs, TooManySameIPs}; TimeoutIP states the wait inside the message text ({ttl} seconds), not in a header.
notes: IP-based: it follows the CALLER'S IP, not the key; rotating keys is useless. The ttl is in prose only (stated_seconds could be parsed, up to 4 days, then a non-numeric variant). Widest scope but the vocabulary has none for IP; credential used as nearest.

message_template: Wrong credentials to submit as this worker. | ...
distinguishing_fields: 403 + rc names the missing privilege.
notes: Worker-side or admin operations; not relevant to a client submitting prompts, but they share status 403 with KudosUpfront.

body.message: Text Waiting Prompt (Status) with ID '<id>' not found. You have requested this URI [...] but did you mean /api/v2/generate/text/status/<string:id> ?

message_template: Text Waiting Prompt (Status) with ID '<id>' not found. ...
distinguishing_fields: 404 + rc "RequestNotFound" (also InvalidJobID, WorkerNotFound, UserNotFound, ThingNotFound).
notes: Real capture. TRAP: retry-after: 60 and x-ratelimit-* are on EVERY response, including this error and 200s; retry-after is a standing hint, not an instruction to wait after a 404. The wait-hint header on a non-429 must not be applied as a rest. A prompt that expired is 410 RequestExpired ("Prompt Request Expired").

distinguishing_fields: 410 + rc "RequestExpired": the queued request timed out waiting for a worker and was cancelled.
notes: Queue/capacity outcome on a crowdsourced pool. Resubmitting may work; not a key or request fault. Using family request_fault is a stretch; the nearest reading is that this is capacity (model_not_ready) for the model.

body.message: Parallel requests ({count}) exceeded user limit ({concurrency}). Please try again later or request to increase your concurrency.

message_template: Parallel requests (<n>) exceeded user limit (<limit>). Please try again later or request to increase your concurrency. | Too many anonymous requests on using the AI Horde currently (<n>/<limit>). ...
distinguishing_fields: 429 + rc "TooManyPrompts": a CONCURRENCY cap on queued/in-flight requests (not per-minute), per user; anonymous variant says "Too many anonymous requests".
notes: The counter drains as jobs finish (seconds to minutes). No window label for concurrency in the vocabulary; window none. No Retry-After meaning beyond the standing header. Another registered key has its own limit (anonymous shares one IP/pool limit).

distinguishing_fields: 429 with remaining 0 and Retry-After; limit/remaining/reset headers present on all responses (limit 60 seen).
sources: first-hand: headers observed on a 404 (limit 60, remaining 59) on 2026-10-16; the 429 itself not triggered
notes: The 429 body and exact trigger were not captured (no requests sent to provoke it). x-ratelimit-reset is an EPOCH timestamp, not seconds: a parser must tell epoch from delta. Per-IP or per-key bucket unknown. Plugin should only trust Retry-After when status is 429.

body.message: No active worker found to fulfill this request. Please Try again later...

message_template: No active worker found to fulfill this request. Please Try again later...
distinguishing_fields: 400 + rc "NoValidWorkers" (source class sets retry_after = 600 in the exception object; whether it is sent as a header was not seen).
notes: TRAP: capacity absence delivered as 400. No worker serves the requested model/size right now; the request itself is fine.

body.message: AI Horde has entered maintenance mode. Please try again later.

message_template: AI Horde has entered maintenance mode. Please try again later.
distinguishing_fields: 400 + rc "MaintenanceMode" (exception retry_after = 60).
notes: Whole service paused; every key fails. 400 status but a server condition. Rotating keys is pointless.

message_template: <text varies, e.g. Too many sampling steps...>
distinguishing_fields: 400 + rc naming the validation (all {message, rc}).
notes: Includes a 400 for NUL bytes in a payload.

distinguishing_fields: 5xx, no rc.
sources: Cloudflare front; horde-node header names the node (e.g. kobold:7006:5.1.14)
notes: No 5xx captures found. Inferred. Response header horde-node identifies the backend node.
